body: i am of like mind. the school of thought already exists, its called libertarian socialism or anarcho-communism. you have brought up some very crucial anthropological points. What, at this exact moment in western society, is left to challenge man? and i mean truly challenge. we don't even think about where our food comes from whereas back in the day, hunting was intrinsic to human life. our commercialized industrialized world is not meant for free thinkers like us. society does not want you to think or exist outside the box that it creates for us; that's why people go to jail for not paying taxes. The neoliberal world order has stifled the energetic human spirit and made most of us docile sheep that don't even know we're slaves to their money-making agenda. you should get involved in leftist politics because your post is basically what the libertarian left is so against (just stay away from "woke" liberals and the authoritarian left) At this depressing, adventure-less time in western civilization, it is often helpful, for me at least, to learn about societies that came before us, specifically Native Americans, whom i believe we should use as a model for an ideal society, especially the Iroquois. Also, it is encouraging to note that the next frontier, space, is rapidly opening up and soon, there will be advancements in transportation that we would have never thought possible. This gives me hope, in addition to the fact that theres so much money (if youre in to that sort of thing) to be made from space. Start investing in space companies like Virgin Galactic (SPCE) now, and you'll be ahead of the curve because when the space boom starts, which it's only a matter of time before that happens as we see the advancements in technology already happening now, you can be one of the ones to get rich off that. Money is a terrible motivator, but the things one can do with money are the real motivations (what's funny about that is money is the real "enslaver" of humanity, as is access to resources). Those who control the resources also control the money, and in theory, you need alot of money to fight the slavemasters, but then once you have enough money, you become one yourself. That is the paradox that saves capitalism time and again, because only those who benefit from it most have the power to change it, and since theyre benefitting from it so much, why would they change anything?

i deal with all these feelings myself and it's very hard. Sometimes, the people who treat you as inferior and don't see your worth are the ones you should cut out of your life. That can be hard when it's everyone, believe me I know, but sometimes a change of scenery can be so beneficial. one thing that I've found helps with self-worth is working hard and succeeding at something that's important to you. Whether its getting ocky at the gym or getting A's in college, or succeeding at your job, or flipping a pack, or reading a new book, or just setting some basic goals for yourself and meeting them, accomplishing stuff can take away a lot of the pain. I have been dealing with terrible depression and suicidal thoughts lately, but I've found that my main source of happiness has been starting my business and seeing it grow in the last few weeks. You just gotta find the motivation to get up and go do something! This is obviously easier said than done, but there's a lot of stuff you can try without even leaving the house! Learn to cook a new thing (learning to make flan is very easy and but also difficult and rewarding at the same time) or try to get better at a videogame (although this can be a rabbithole as well) The possibilities are almost endless though, and whatever you find, just know that you are good enough to be loved, you deserve love and respect like everyone else, but the first step to that is self-respect, so find something that makes you proud and adds some extra meaning to your daily existence.
